name: No Diagnosis
statement: No diagnosis. A reel can explain what a symptom may mean. It cannot tell someone what they have.
rationale: A reel can explain what a symptom may mean, but cannot tell a viewer what they individually have.
enforcement: Prohibit diagnostic statements such as 'You have condition X'. Require probabilistic language ('This could indicate', 'Common reasons include').

name: No Dosages, Brand Names, or Prescribing
statement: No dosages, no brand names, no prescribing. Not even in passing, not even for common drugs.
rationale: Not even in passing, not even for common over-the-counter drugs.
enforcement: Strictly filter out specific medication brands, milligram dosages, and prescription directives.

name: Mandatory Clinical Consultation Threshold
statement: Always include a threshold that sends the viewer to a real consultation. Some sign, duration or combination that means see someone in person.
rationale: Every script must provide a clear boundary condition that tells the patient when to seek in-person medical care.
enforcement: Ensure script contains an explicit threshold (e.g. duration > 2 weeks, specific red-flag combination) directing viewers to a doctor.

name: No Identifiable Patient Details
statement: No identifiable patient details. Change the details in any case story, and never use photographs or names.
rationale: Patient privacy and medical ethics require total anonymization.
enforcement: Ensure all case stories change biographical details, omit hospital names/dates, and avoid identifiable personal histories.

name: One Call-To-Action (CTA) Per Reel
statement: One call to action per reel. Three CTAs produce fewer results than one.
rationale: Three CTAs produce fewer results than one. Asking to comment, save, and share simultaneously ruins conversion.
enforcement: Strictly enforce a single, focused CTA at the conclusion.

name: Three-Second Hook Primacy
statement: The first three seconds decide everything. Whatever framework you pick, the opening line carries most of the weight.
rationale: The first three seconds decide whether the viewer scrolls away or watches the entire reel.
enforcement: The opening line must immediately establish tension, curiosity, a direct group callout, or a sharp surprising statement.
